plan.output: A reviewable table of extracted game-test rows with likely duplicate rows flagged for a tester to inspect.
inputs: A synthetic CSV containing session time, device, battery, temperature, frame-drop count and note
A tester-selected set of fields to compare when identifying likely repeats
plan.trigger: An operator manually supplies a completed CSV file for one review run.
steps: Extract the supplied CSV into row records.
Check that required test columns are present and flag missing values.
Compare rows using the operator-selected fields.
Mark matching rows as possible repeats without deleting them.
Produce a review table and a short count of flagged rows.
Have the tester verify all flags before using or importing any row.
plan.acceptanceCheck: On a synthetic file with labeled required fields and known repeated rows, verify that extraction preserves each supplied value and that only rows matching the selected comparison fields are flagged.
plan.humanBoundary: The tester supplies and checks the CSV, chooses fields that define a duplicate, verifies flagged rows, and handles any live upload or sheet import; the prototype must not silently discard records.

plan.output: A dated comparison table that flags differing supplied purchase totals and lists possible explanations for human review.
inputs: Synthetic daily Shopify order totals with channel and test/cancelled-order labels
Synthetic daily Meta purchase totals labeled with the selected attribution window
An operator-supplied date range and column mapping
plan.trigger: An operator manually provides two matching date-range tables for a review run.
steps: Check that both tables cover the same dates.
Apply the supplied channel, test-order and attribution labels.
Compare totals by date and mark mismatches.
Show the comparison with a neutral note that attribution methods can differ.
Flag patterns for investigation without diagnosing their cause.
Have a merchant verify the exports and inspect tracking settings independently.
plan.acceptanceCheck: For a synthetic pair of tables with known dates and totals, confirm that aligned dates are compared correctly, mismatched totals are marked, and the output does not label a difference as a duplicate sale without human verification.
plan.humanBoundary: A merchant exports and maps both tables, confirms filters and attribution settings, investigates any flagged date, and decides whether tracking needs changes; the prototype does not access a store or alter tracking.

Whether flags help distinguish ordinary attribution differences from tracking errors
Whether any merchant would pay for this review
